options.label: e

expl: To define the constitutional amendment procedure, Article 368 of Part XX of the Constitution of India provides for three types of amendments— (i) By simple majority (ii) By special majority of Parliament (iii) By special majority of Parliament along with the ratification by the legislatures of at least half of the States.

stem: Creation of a new state requires a ....... majority for Constitutional Amendment.

options.label: d
options.text: Two-third plus ratification by half of all states

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: For the creation of new States, the special procedure under Article 368 (constitutional amendment procedure) is not adopted. Parliament can create new States by a simple majority, and as per Article 4(2), such a law is not deemed to be an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.

stem: Which constitutional amendment gave Delhi the name national Capital Territory?
expl: Under the new Article 239AA inserted by the 69th Constitution (Amendment) Act, 1991, the Union Territory of Delhi was named the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi and its administrator was designated as the Lieutenant Governor. Along with this, provisions were also made for the establishment of a Legislative Assembly for the NCT of Delhi and a Council of Ministers responsible to it.

stem: A Bill for the amendment in Indian Constitution can be presented -

options.label: c
options.text: Either in Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha

options.label: d
options.text: In the Supreme Court of India

expl: A Bill for amendment of the Indian Constitution can be introduced in either House of Parliament—Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha. The amending power and the procedure for it are described in Article 368 of the Constitution.

stem: When was the first Bill for the amendment of the Indian Constitution presented?
expl: The Constitution (First Amendment) Bill was introduced in 1951. Through this amendment, Articles 15, 19, 85, 87, 174, 176, 341, 342, 372 and 376 were amended, and two new Articles 31-A and 31-B, along with the 9th Schedule, were added to the Constitution.

stem: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts was termed as Mini Constitution?
expl: By the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, an attempt was made to change many fundamental provisions of the Constitution. Therefore, it was termed the “Mini-Constitution”.

stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution of India:
1. It added three words to the Preamble—‘Socialist’, ‘Secular’ and ‘Integrity’.
2. It added eight Fundamental Duties to the Constitution.
3. It added new Directive Principles, i.e., Article 39A, Article 43A and Article 47.
4. It granted power to the President, in consultation with the Election Commission, to disqualify members of the State legislatures.
Which of the above statements are incorrect?
expl: • The Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976 brought changes in many provisions of the Constitution and also added several new provisions. Hence, it is called the “Mini-Constitution”. Through it, the following provisions were added or amended— • It added three new words in the Preamble— Socialist, Secular and Integrity. • It added 10 Fundamental Duties in the Constitution. • Three new Directive Principles were added— equal justice and free legal aid (Article 39A), participation of workers in the management of industries (Article 43A), and protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife (Article 48A). • By substituting Article 192, it provided the President with the power to disqualify members of State Legislative Assemblies/Councils on the advice of the Election Commission; however, by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, this power was again given to the Governor. Thus, in the given statements, statements 1 and 4 are correct, while statements 2 and 3 are incorrect.

stem: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment in India has decided the maximum strength of the Council of Minister with Chief Minister in a State ?
expl: Under Clause (1A) added to Article 164 by the Constitution (Ninety-first Amendment) Act, 2003, it is provided that the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a State’s Council of Ministers shall not exceed fifteen (15) percent of the total strength of the State Legislative Assembly; however, in a State, the number of ministers including the Chief Minister shall not be less than twelve (12).
